y01-b.motion: Locked camera fixed in the back seat, moving with the car; no zoom, pan or tilt. The car is already rolling fast. From the first moment the driver on the left hauls the wheel hard left with both gloved hands, his shoulders and elbows leaning into the turn; the heavy car body rolls on its springs and both men sway with it, then settle as it straightens. Through the windscreen the brick street swings and slides past. Both men keep facing forward. The masks and the grey hat stay exactly as they are: white ring, red triangle, no holes. Engine roar, tyres drumming on cobbles. No speech.

y02-a.motion: Locked camera low at the wet kerb; no zoom, pan or tilt. The car is already sliding broadside, its rear wheel spinning in place and pouring thick white smoke that rolls left along the cobbles. The heavy car slides only a short way right, staying in frame, then the tyre grips and the body rocks once on its springs and settles. The man leaning from the window keeps the gun pointed straight up at the sky in both gloved hands and pumps it upward twice, head steady toward the lens. The driver stays at the wheel. Both masks stay exactly as they are: white ring, red triangle, no holes. Tyre screech, engine.

y03-a.motion: Slow motion, locked camera; no zoom, pan or tilt. He keeps flying sideways through the air, travelling only a little to the right and sinking slightly as gravity takes him, his cream jacket flapping and his trouser legs rippling. He holds the gun pointed straight up at the ceiling in both gloved hands the whole time. His head stays square to the lens and large in frame. Behind him glass crystals fall steadily, glint in the window light and bounce off the marble counter. The mask stays exactly as it is: white ring, red triangle, no holes. Tinkling glass, cloth snapping. No speech.

y04-a.motion: Locked-off camera, tripod-stable, no zoom, pan or tilt; one continuous shot. The man stands still in the window frame of the fallen house front. At once his gloved hand brushes the dust off his lapel in two firm strokes, then he squares his shoulders, tugs his jacket straight with one hand and sets his feet, the carpet bag held steady at his side. A last puff of plaster dust settles round his boots. His head stays square to the lens throughout; his knitted mask does not change. Sound: settling timber creaks, a cloth brush, a distant dog.

y05-a.motion: Locked-off camera, tripod-stable, no zoom, pan or tilt; one continuous shot. The man leans on the standing barrel with both gloved hands flat on its rim. Whiskey keeps glugging from the split barrel at his feet and spreads slowly across the cobbles in a widening amber puddle. He straightens his back, plants both hands on the barrel lid and gives it one firm, heavy pat, then rests there, deadpan. His head stays still, angled down at the spill; his knitted mask does not change. Sound: liquid gurgling, a dull wooden thump.

y06-a.motion: Locked-off camera, tripod-stable, no zoom, pan or tilt; one continuous shot. The two men hold the canvas sack between them over the basket rim and give it two hard, shared shakes, so a thick stream of banknotes tumbles out and flutters away down towards the clouds. On the third beat they lift the empty sack and hold it out flat, deadpan, facing the lens. Their heads stay square to the camera and do not turn; both knitted masks stay exactly as they are. The ropes sway a little. Sound: wind, flapping paper, creaking wicker.

p03y-b.motion: Locked-off camera, no zoom, pan or tilt; one continuous shot. He stays standing in place behind the counter, facing the lens, head nearly still. On the first beat his shrug drops and pops back up, gloved palms bouncing; on the next both arms swing in and slap flat on the counter; then one palm sweeps sideways towards the old woman, presenting her; then a big double shrug again, shoulders to his ears. Hands stay below the mask. The old woman sips her coffee, unimpressed. His mask stays exactly as in the first frame: white ring, one red triangle, no holes. Diner hum, palm slaps.

z06y-b.motion: Locked-off camera, no zoom, pan or tilt; one continuous shot. The two men stand upright either side of the safe, heads facing the lens. On the first beat the man in the mustard suit raps the safe's top twice with his gloved knuckles; on the next he pats it like a prize horse; then his free hand points down at it and back to his own chest. The man in brown tweed rocks the sack truck a little on its wheels, the safe tilting, and nods on the beat. Masks stay exactly as in the first frame: white ring, one red triangle, no holes. g08y-b.motion: Locked-off camera, no zoom, pan or tilt; one continuous shot. The big gloved hand in the foreground stays up, fingers spread, never passing over his face: on each beat it wiggles its fingers like a stage magician, then snaps them, then waves slowly side to side. Behind his back, in plain view, his other hand keeps slowly pushing the folded banknote deeper into his jacket pocket until it is gone inside. His head stays where it is, tilted showily, facing the lens. His mask stays exactly as in the first frame: white ring, one red triangle, no holes. Smoke drifts in the spotlight. A finger snap, cloth rustle.

v05y-a.motion: Locked-off camera, no zoom, pan or tilt; one continuous shot. He stays planted in his crouch, facing the lens, head square, no spin. On the first beat his lower glove chops down through the air; on the next his raised thumb jabs back over his shoulder at the man on the lever; then both fists pump at chest height twice; then the chop again, harder. His knees bounce on every beat. Hands stay clear of his face. His mask stays exactly as in the first frame: white ring, one red triangle, no holes. The owner hauls the lever, the workers shrink back. Furnace roar, flywheels turning.
